title: introduce resumable checkpoint streaming protocol and ergonomic SDK helpers across py/ts/go
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Production streaming workloads occasionally need to resume long-lived streams after transient disconnects without replaying the entire conversation. This PR implements a lightweight resumable/checkpoint hinting protocol (session-checkpoint v0.1) and exposes ergonomic helpers in all three SDKs so product teams can opt-in with minimal code changes. Summary of changes: 1) Protocol: introduce an optional 'X-Session-Checkpoint' header and resumable token semantics returned on streaming completion (response metadata). Server will emit stable checkpoint tokens that encode minimal KV cursor + prefix hash; clients can pass checkpoint token on a new stream to resume from that point where supported. 2) SDK surface: Python: add AsyncResumeableStream and helper resume_from_checkpoint(checkpoint: str) on StreamingClient; TypeScript: augment createStream({ resumeToken?: string }) and add generator helper stream.resumeWith(token); Go: introduce ReaderWithCheckpoint and streaming.ResumeFrom(token string) convenience wrapper. 3) Retries/backoff: align retry windows when resuming so clients don't double-retry content; introduce 'jitter_scale' in retry presets and expose opt-in PWM (progress-weighted multiplier) so resumption retries favor shorter windows for resumption flows. 4) Ergonomics/parity: ensure all three SDKs provide an idiomatic way to accept a checkpoint token and return one on normal completion or explicit checkpoint() call. 5) Docs & examples: cross-SDK quickstarts and a migration guide. Commits (high level): - Add protocol docs + OpenAPI extension for X-Session-Checkpoint header - Implement server side checkpoint generator and validation (small shim) - Add Python AsyncResumeableStream + unit tests - Add TS generator helpers + typed resumeToken types + e2e test - Add Go ReaderWithCheckpoint and examples + integration test - Add retry presets and jitter_scale implementation for client-side resume flow - Update changelogs and quickstart examples - Add CI job to run tri-sdk resume e2e matrix Changed files (high level): server/api/streaming_spec.yaml, server/handlers/checkpoint.go, sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py, sdk/python/tests/test_resume.py, sdk/typescript/src/stream.ts, sdk/typescript/tests/resume.spec.ts, sdk/go/stream_resume.go, docs/guides/resumable_streams.md, examples/multi-sdk/resume_quickstart.md, changelogs/py-0.19.0.md, changelogs/ts-1.30.0.md, changelogs/go-1.9.0.md. Testing notes: added targeted unit tests in each SDK and a small end-to-end CI matrix that spins a local handler-sim (lightweight checkpoint mock) and validates resume semantics under network jitter. CI initially failed on a flaky TS e2e due to an intermittent timing assumption; fixed by switching to a polling-based resume readiness probe and re-ran. Backwards compatibility: The transport change is opt-in — servers only emit X-Session-Checkpoint when checkpointing enabled; old clients ignore unknown headers. Clients that want resume must explicitly opt-in via the new helper surfaces. Rollout: feature-flagged on server side; SDK helpers are behind minor versions and documented. Migration: minimal — example included for each SDK. Usage examples (short): Python: stream = client.stream(...); cp = stream.checkpoint(); resumed = client.resume_from_checkpoint(cp) TypeScript: const stream = client.createStream(); const cp = await stream.checkpoint(); await client.createStream({resumeToken: cp}) Go: r := sdk.NewResumeReader(...); token := r.Checkpoint(); resumed, _ := sdk.ResumeFrom(token) Security notes: checkpoint tokens are opaque signed blobs (HMAC) - servers validate; no user data returned in token. Release bumps: python 0.19.0, typescript 1.30.0, go 1.9.0. Links: Linear ENG-2109 for protocol design; SUP-1123 incident that motivated resumption.
review_comments: Marco Li: Nice, this addresses the SUP-1123 replay storm risk. Two requests: ensure we document expected size/entropy of tokens and add a defensive server-side TTL for tokens.
Aisha Patel (author): Added token TTL enforcement on server (checkpoint.go) and a short section in docs about size/entropy. Tokens are HMAC-signed 48 bytes base64 by default.

Dana Roberts: TS helper API looks good; one nit: prefer resumeToken over token in parameter names for discoverability. Also, can we expose a 'resumeable' boolean on the stream object for feature gating in client code?
Aisha Patel (author): Renamed parameter to resumeToken and added stream.resumeable boolean on TS/py/go stream objects. Update tests accordingly.
Evan Kim: Tests look solid. Suggest adding a test for retry/jitter behavior when resume is used in hot paths — otherwise approving.
Aisha Patel (author): Added resume-specific retry test with jitter_scale=0.6 to the e2e matrix as requested.
release_notes: Introduce optional resumable streaming via session checkpoints. SDKs: Python 0.19.0, TypeScript 1.30.0, Go 1.9.0 provide ergonomic helpers to create, checkpoint, and resume streams. Opt-in feature; see docs/guides/resumable_streams.md for migration steps and security considerations.
